newsitem.title: USA: CRITEF partners says file order vs Dominium.
newsitem.headline: CRITEF partners says file order vs Dominium.

text.p: The general partners of two CRITEF partnerships said on Friday they filed for a restraining order against Dominium Tax Exempt Fund LLP, alleging the fund violated Federal securities law.

There are two CRITEF partnerships with three series of securities that trade on the American Stock Exchange -- Capital Realty Investors Tax Exempt Limited Partnership and Capital Realty Investors Tax Exempt Fund III Limited Partnership.

The partners, who filed for the restraining order with prospective merger partner Capital Apartment Properties Inc, said in a statement Dominium allegedly violated securities law in its efforts to impede a proposed merger between the CRITEF partnerships and affiliates of Capital Apartment.

The suit charged Dominium violated securities law by sending a letter and issuing a press release constituting proxy solicitations to investors in the CRITEF partnerships before delivering more detailed preliminary proxy material to investors, CRITEF said.
The suit also charged that the letter and press release contained false and misleading statements about proposed mergers between CRITEF partnerships and Capital affiliates, CRITEF said.

As a result, CRITEF said its suit sought to restrain Dominium from communicating further with CRITEF Beneficial Assignee Certificates holders until Dominium delivered a proper proxy statement in compliance with U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission rules to them.
Privately-held real estate developer Dominium was not immediately available for comment.
Dominium said on October 1 it filed the proxy material as part of its efforts to block the proposed merger of the two partnerships into privately-held Capital Apartment Properties.
It said in the proxy materials it argued the general partners of the funds were not acting to maximize value for the securities holders.

CRITEF, which filed the suit in U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York, said the suit also sought compensatory and punitive damages for Dominium's alleged tortious interference with the merger contracts.
CRITEF alleged Dominium tried for seven months to come up with a proposal that would exceed Capital's offer of about $160 million but failed to obtain firm financing.

William Dockser, chairman of CRI Inc, managing general partner of the CRITEF partnerships, said: "We stand behind the merger proposals and recommend that the BAC holders vote yes on all of the questions on the proxies. Neither Dominium nor anyone else has been able to beat CAPREIT's (Capital's) offer."
